raw.description:
Sinai Sound System is a Sheffield-based sound system rooted in the UK dub and steppers tradition, carrying forward the lineage of Iration Steppas. Operating one of the UK and Europe’s most impressive and sought-after rigs, Sinai moves between heavyweight roots, dub, and bass music, with Spanish vocalist Lasai bringing his own reggae and dancehall influence and live mic energy to the session.

Queen Majesty has been a fixture in NYC’s reggae and sound system scene for more than two decades, known for deep selections across roots, dub, and dancehall.

About Echo Chamber:

Echo Chamber returns in 2026, rebooting Dub-Stuy's long-running series, first launched in 2012, as an ongoing residency at Public Records. Hosted on select Thursdays in the Sound Room, the series centers sound, system, and the dancefloor as spaces for open listening and exploration.

Programming traces a wide musical arc from Jamaica to the UK and New York, moving fluidly from foundation reggae and dub into dub techno, dubstep, drum & bass, and global bass, connecting lineage with future-facing sounds. Powered by Public Records' bass-forward quadraphonic system, each session pairs Dub-Stuy resident DJs with special guests from the global sound system community.

\-

Public Records aims to provide a safer space. We reject all forms of discrimination, including racism, misogyny, transphobia, homophobia, sexism, and other aggressive behavior. Consent is paramount. Please exist with respect for yourself and those around you. Anyone found in violation of our rules or safer space policy will be removed from the venue.

To share feedback about an incident, please email hello@publicrecords.nyc or alert a member of our team.

Tickets may be available at the door based on capacity. A ticket does not guarantee entry; Public Records reserves the right to deny entry to guests that appear intoxicated or do not meet the dress code. All large bags and coats must be checked. Doors close one hour before end time.

highlights.title: Presented by SILO Brooklyn & BUSH DÜF.

raw.description:
BUSH DÜF makes a triumphant return to our favorite Danley sound system with a venerable lineup of local DJs. Featuring a mix of first-timers at SILO and previous party presiders in a much-anticipated big-room b2b, expect another astounding night of cosmic, colorful and cathartic techno till the fog and floor must clear.

SUPER WAV treats us to a techno-tilted opener as our first SILO debut. A music-lover in every regard, he wields a wide-ranging palette spanning psychedelic house, jackin’ acid and many genres defying easy categorization. Evoking the universal in even the most esoteric sounds, his thoughtful curation scouts selections and selectors alike as the organizer of ripple worldwide, a downtempo mix series, and synchroNYCity, a recently-established party built around revisitations of timeless records.

EMMALINE then takes us to midnight and beyond with her propensity for expressive propulsion. The driving force behind Bossa-based BUCKLE UP BABY is more than just a hostess of high-energy rhythms, but a consistently-mesmerizing mixer of dense layers and direct emotion, seamlessly navigating improvisation and authorship. Her acoustic acumen is not to be missed on a sound system like SILO’s, which is why we’re thrilled she could join our party for the first time in what is also her venue debut.

Ben Zo and STEEN are back with their biggest b2b yet. Each attuned to the nuances to the stadium-sized sound system at-hand, their respective experiences as DÜF director and Open Decks ombudsman promise unique uplift in this space familiar to both. Reprising their b2b after a few months instead of a few years like before, their symbiosis as selectors dates back half a decade (to when they first met at STEEN's open decks) and today finds its broadest canvass yet with six decks between them and several points of sound around them.

Dio García returns to the DÜF after a few years away with his unrestrained range and freewheeling finesse. With roots in Miami and branches touching upon many of Brooklyn's seminal parties, the Acid Mama co-organizer and Xanadu production manager is a dependably heady architect of groovy and glistening set construction spanning animated acid, blistering bass, dubby and deep house, quintessentially Detroit techno and more. We're eager to have him as the final venue debutant, and in the main room, no less.

raw.description:
Join us with Sam Allan and Lukas Frank on the rooftop of Superior Ingredients for an unforgettable night of Afro Melodic progresssive house. Vibes high, beats deep, and the city skyline as your backdrop.

BIOGRAPHY

Lukas & Frank is a dynamic DJ duo established in late 2024, blending the unexpected and making it work in all the right ways. Lukas plays live Sax, Frank plays live Cello - but that's just the beginning. Lukas comes from a classical background, having studied clarinet before switching to the saxophone and starting out as a DJ. Frank grew up with classical music but moved then to rock and techno, channeling his energy through his cello. Two friends from totally different musical worlds - and yet, something clicked. It all started when they were booked separately for a gig without a clue what to play. What followed was pure intuition: Sax and Cello melting into grooves of Afro and Melodic House. The crowd went wild - and Lukas & Frank was born.

• House of LUKAS & FRANK (HOLF), an exclusive in-house event series spanning Berlin, London, Paris, Istanbul, Sofia and other global cities.

Sam Allan is one of New York's most dynamic forces in electronic music. Blending progressive, afro and melodic, house influences, Sam crafts emotionally charged records built for peak-hour dancefloors.

raw.description:
A full hotel takeover by Robot Heart & Ashram Galactica.

**Message the concierge for group tickets, private suites, and our exclusive hotel booking code: concierge@checkincheckout.nyc**

Across 3 days and 2 nights our hotel will become a fever dream of music, mischief and unexpected encounters:

- Friday 6PM-10PM - Warm Up with Ashram Galactica
- Friday 10PM-4AM - Robot Heart takes the lead. Chetana hosts a secret room.
- Saturday 2PM-10PM - Wake Up Call with Ashram Galactica
- Saturday 10PM-4AM - Robot Heart full takeover
- Sunday 4AM - Late - Afterhours.

Intimate, immersive, and filled with love and beats.

You may join us for individual events, or the full weekend.

🗝️

Now, let's talk about what you're wearing:

BY NIGHT · DOWNTOWN AFTER DARK

Robot Heart takes us into late ’70s and early ’80s New York: Punk meets disco and hotel glamour. Think sharp suits, leather, silk, velvet, lamé, gold, a flash of red and one detail that makes the look yours. Sexy, stylish and a little rebellious. Look through the NIGHT Mood Board here: https://pin.it/IIxxGb3nB

BY DAY - THE WAKE UP CALL

Roll out of bed late and show up in your best sleep attire. Silk pajamas, slips, gowns, kaftans and robes + slippers meet Ashram Galactica’s main tent vibes for a daytime dance party. Classic NYC brunch items served. Look through the DAY Mood Board here: https://pin.it/60XETUqM1

THE MUSIC

We won't be announcing the artists. But we will give hints...

FRIDAY - We welcome one half of an iconic New York duo that broke Nas, Biggie, Jay-Z and Wu-Tang before any of them had deals. This musicologist is going to take you on a sonic journey from the 70s-90s with his priceless collection.

Next up - two legendary figures of New York City dance music come together for a rare, extended journey through house, disco, soul, and deep underground grooves. Both have spent decades shaping the sound and culture of the city. Not simply as DJs, but as selectors, tastemakers, and architects of some of New York’s most influential dance floors

Finally - a Tel Aviv duo who came up through punk, never put the guitars away and infused it into their distinctive sound.

SATURDAY - Has anyone been to Marcy Hotel? The Brooklyn loft that slowed house music down.

Plus, the Godfather of disco house.

And finally, a Robot Heart breakout star, and an All Day I Dream staple.

From pioneers to future stars, it all traces back to the origins.

Full Weekend Passes & Single Day/Night tickets are available

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Is… someone watching you? Are you seeing that face again? The nightmares are back, aren’t they. Make your appointment, the symptoms aren’t slowing down.

Night One of our four party series descends below what you thought you knew. Tonight, the impulses you keep locked away run wild - rampant and unapologetic.

Dress as the obsession gnawing on the flesh of your brain, your fears of what’s under the bed, or the animal inside of you.

In CARGO, Serrian initiates the unraveling from 9PM–11:30PM, followed by Rose Kourts from 11:30PM–1:30AM, welcoming that distorted pleasure many shy away from.

Then, Lauren Flax takes control from 1:30AM–3:30AM. Detroit-born and Brooklyn-forged, Flax has spent more than two decades moving through the darkest alleys of techno, electro, house, and jungle. Unrelenting, she drives CARGO past the point of reason until raw instinct is the only thing left.

The Foyer isn’t safe either; with Lady Harley ramping us up from 9:00PM-12:00AM. Once the clock strikes midnight, Catladyhi takes over until 3AM, with a carnal need to facilitate psychic release.

Over in the Porch, Bea Trinidad and ellen.j take over—because there’s nowhere left to hide.

PSYCHOSIS is a reckoning. The twisted thoughts that live in the back of our minds come crawling out, the stages of grief are embodied in flesh, and together, we face our demons before they find us first.

Kitchen open late. Coat check available. 21+.

All ticket sales are final

We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Club Joon is taking over Halloween in New York.

Club Joon is a community party rooted in Persian, SWANA and MENA culture, bringing people together through music, food, dancing and real-life connection. Whether you grew up with the music or you’re experiencing it for the first time, you’re invited.

For Halloween, we’re giving Club Joon a spooky little twist. Expect a packed dance floor, DJs all night, costumes, surprises, and a room full of people ready to dance, meet someone new and celebrate together.

Come ready to dance.

Everyone is welcome.

⫸ LOOKS

Halloween at Club Joon means more than just a dance floor.

Come with your friends or come ready to make new ones.

⫸ WHAT IS CLUB JOON?

“Joon” is a Persian term of endearment meaning something like “my love” or “my soul.”

Club Joon is a NYC-based community event centered around Persian, SWANA and MENA music, culture and connection. Our parties are about getting people off their phones and into the same room to dance, meet new people, celebrate culture and connect in real life.

While Club Joon is rooted in our community, you don’t have to be Persian, SWANA or MENA to be part of it.

If you come with love, you’re a Joon.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Alix Perez (Belgium/UK) and Eprom (USA) are **SHADES**.

Perez found his rise to fame in drum n bass, releasing on Shogun Audio, Exit Recordings amongst many other labels and collaborating with the foremost names in dance and electronic music such as Noisia, Foreign Beggars, dBridge, and many more.

Eprom gained his well-deserved success through his innovative take on bass music, a unique sound that has the likes of Gaslamp Killer, Kutmah, D-Styles singing his praises and supporting his music.

SHADES exemplifies slanted grooves, a deep pocket and hard yet graceful composition. The debut self-titled EP (released on Alpha Pup) is a truly unique body of work.

Aware of each other’s music for some time before meeting, Perez and Eprom first crossed paths at the 2013/2014 Northern Bass festival in New Zealand. The following summer they met again at the Red Bull Studios LA producing the Foreign Beggars’ Modus EP. This initial studio session led to further collaborations and SHADES was born.

XLR8R have rightly said “music that’s not only a legitimate full-frontal assault in the same vein as tunes from that golden era of gluttonous bass and synths, but that embraces that ethos while giving it a more polished feel”.

raw.description:
Halloween Night & Day at Signal stretches from Friday through Sunday morning moving through every corner of club music.

Friday begins with a special Shelter x Signal collaboration, featuring global fixture Apollonia. The trio of Dan Ghenacia, Dyed Soundorom and Shonky have spent more than a decade refining their unmistakable approach to house: deep, stripped-back and relentlessly groovy, built for long sets where records are given room to unfold. Their shared history behind the decks makes them a natural fit for an extended Halloween set.

Across the weekend, Berghain mainstay PARAMIDA brings the freewheeling spirit of Love On The Rocks, where house, trance, acid, proto-dance and stranger corners of the dancefloor collide. Inner Lakes pushes into psychedelic territory, folding breaks, techno and progressive electronics into his distinctly tripped-out sound, while Bristol’s Hodge brings rhythmic pressure and bass-weight experimentation.

Jade Seatle joins with her sharp, fast-moving approach to techno and trance, alongside Karine’s deep and hypnotic selections and Shakolin, a defining voice of Kyiv’s underground whose sets move fluidly through house, techno, electro and the spaces between.

They’re joined across the marathon by Alvaro Medina, Bobby., Chloe Battelle, deep creep, Henry Chow, J. Richards, Jack Mulqueen, Joiah, Julie Marghilano, Kurilo, Mathew Jonson (Live), Matthias, Nuno Carneiro, Per Hammar, So-Fi, Taimur, Tommy Chikara, Vitess, Wayne Holland and 98dots.

We're excited to host a very special Halloween event inside of one New York City's oldest Courthouses featuring Distant Matter in the heart of Tribeca.

All tickets include admission and an open vodka & tequila bar from 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.

This event space features two different floors and we will bringing in top notch customized production and decor to create a very special curated Halloween night. We will have food & drink available, halloween costumes are encouraged but not mandatory.

The 31 Chambers Courthouse, also known as the Surrogate's Courthouse, is an architectural gem located in Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 1907, this Beaux-Arts style building is known for its grand facade adorned with intricate sculptures and its richly decorated interiors. It houses the Surrogate's Court of New York County, which handles probate and estate matters. The courthouse's presence and historical significance make it a notable landmark in New York City.

This is a strict 21+ event.

Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

There's a midnight costume contest with champagne prize, so be sure to arrive early.

**Maesic** is quickly becoming one of the most exciting names in next-gen dance music. London born and raised in the south of France, the versatile producer and DJ is known for seamlessly blending multiple genres of dance music, including tech-house, EDM, Afro House, and melodic techno. His distinct sound draws from global club culture and forward-looking innovation.

Maesic began producing music at age 12 and built an early fanbase online. In 2019, he released his debut single, “There In The Morning,” which charted on Spotify France’s Top  200. He was also nominated by DJ Mag France as “Best New Talent” in 2019. Between 2020 and 2022, Maesic broadened his reach as a producer. He also joined forces with Diplo and contributed to Major Lazer projects, working alongside artists like ANYMA, Dillon Francis, Wax Motif, and Blond:ish.

In 2023, Maesic’s singles gained support from Diplo, Fisher, and Malaa. By 2024, he introduced a bold new sound—fusing afro house and techno—collaborating with names like Bob Sinclar, Hugel, and Disco Lines.

2025 marked his breakout moment with the viral hit “Life Is Simple (Move Your Body)” featuring house music legend Marshall Jefferson and Salomé Das. In addition to amassing 85M+ global streams, charting on Spotify’s Global Viral 50 and US Viral 50, the track was crowned the #1 Afro House track of 2025 on Beatport.

Looking ahead, Maesic is preparing a wave of new music, including forthcoming collaborations with some of the biggest names in dance.

**A Funeral for Your Former Self**

The story begins with a cup of “Meng Po’s Soup.”

Drink it, and for one night, leave behind your name, your identity, and the stories you’re ready to release.

Then walk downstairs.

Enter another world.

Five artists will transform the space through installation, visual art, live performance, and interactive moments—each offering their own interpretation of life, death, memory, and rebirth.

Move through the rooms.

Pause. Watch. Explore.

Here, you are not only the audience.

You are part of the story.

✦ THE FAREWELL

This funeral is not for someone else.

It is for an older version of yourself.

A relationship that ended.

An identity that no longer fits.

A life you are ready to leave behind.

✦ THE REBIRTH

After the farewell, the music continues.

The exhibition transforms into a Halloween underground party—because every ending deserves a new beginning.

Bury the old version.

Dance into the next.

This Halloween, the West Village slips into something a little more seductive.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.

If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

Once again the debaucherous spirit of **SILOWEEN** descends upon the Scott Ave. rave cul-de-sac. This Saturday night edition features darker, harder, driving techno from Xenia, Firebunny, and Steen.

There's a midnight costume contest with champagne prize, so be sure to arrive early.

**Xenia**  
Born in the serene confines of a quiet Ukrainian village, Xenia's love for music started in her early years which led her path as a DJ with a residency at the famous Heaven Club in Kyiv. She first got into making and mixing music that complimented acid sounds with a classic techno feel. As she kept at it, her music began to hit harder, slowly turning into a darker kind of hard techno that gets a crowd moving. This shift in style led to her starting her own label in 2024 “Fire Mode” where she's all about pushing the boundaries of hard industrial techno, shifting out from a more comercial side of this sound that we may see consistently. Showcasing her own productions, as well as upcoming and established artists, the goal is for the music to stand out on itself.

For years now, Xenia has been known far and wide as an international touring DJ. From Australia to Brazil, Europe to South Africa, Thailand to South America, we can see her in some of the biggest festivals of 2024, like closing the Dreambeach Festival main stage, Verknipt, Ikarus, Echelon, Sunice (to name a few), as well as hitting up some of the best clubs in the world, such as, Fabrik, Gotec, E1, Gate 13, Nordstern, Input, Bolgia, etc… bringing her unique sound to fans everywhere.

value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Brutalismus 3000 headlines a special edition of RUSH alongside SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera, and Nurse (Body Bag) on Nov 6.

The German duo has exploded onto the global stage with a singularly unhinged take on the rave-techno-hardcore continuum. Fusing gabber and schranz with hyperpop-worthy hooks and a sense of punk populism inherited from artists like The Prodigy, Brutalismus 3000 land like a sledgehammer against the stifling forces of conformity.

SPFDJ makes her long-awaited RUSH debut. The Herrensauna resident and Intrepid Skin label boss is one of the most notorious DJs working today. Her singular mix of raw, thundering techno, tweaked, wired club sounds, fearless rave moments and cheeky vocal flips has made her a figurehead for a generation of artists who dare to reimagine clubbing through a defiant, punk lens. Surf Gang's Eera is one of the driving forces behind the modern wave of hyper-blended electronic music, where trance, hardcore, emo and much more swirl together in a vivid tapestry.

Neo-pop diva Dorian Electra joins with a special DJ set. They arrive fresh off the release of their new self-titled LP, a run of covers that reimagines ten classic songs through a manic, high-speed filter. Finally, Body Bag affiliate Nurse ramps up the BPM to dangerous levels. The Body Bag tagline promises "grotesque hardcore" - Nurse delivers.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Postponement: If an event is rescheduled ticket-holders typically have two options:

Cosmic Gate takes over Superior Ingredients Rooftop on Sunday, November 8, joined by Sinca, Derya Zor, sunrYse, and 4YÛ.

For more than 27 years, German artist Nic Chagall has built Cosmic Gate into one of trance’s most recognized names. His catalog includes genre classics “Fire Wire” and “Exploration of Space,” alongside fan favorites such as “am2pm,” “Fall Into You,” “Nothing To Hide,” and “Your Mind.”

GRAMMY-nominated and once named the highest climber in DJ Mag’s Top 100, Cosmic Gate has performed at Tomorrowland, EDC, Ultra, Creamfields, Dreamstate, Transmission, and A State of Trance. His remix catalog includes music from Armin van Buuren, Tiësto, deadmau5, Above & Beyond, and Gabriel & Dresden. He also runs Wake Your Mind Records and hosts the weekly WYM Radio show.

Joining him is Montréal DJ and producer Sinca, whose sets move between progressive house, classic house, minimal, and indie dance. Her music has appeared on Purified, Bedrock, Anjunadeep, All Day I Dream, and Days Like Nights, with performances at Coachella’s Do LaB, Burning Man, SXM Festival, Stereo Montréal, Brooklyn Mirage, and Akasha Ibiza.

Local artists Derya Zor, sunrYse, and 4YÛ complete the lineup for a Sunday above Brooklyn.

🛼 About Weekend Warm-Up (skate) 🛼

***Come roll out the week’s stress and warm up for everything the weekend has in store. Your weekend starts at Xanadu every Friday from 4-7pm. Consider us your end of week workout and pre-game for the weekend ahead. We got you!***

Vibe and skate to the music of Top 40, R&B

Booth reservations are available for parties 7+ via form: https://www.xanadu.nyc/booking

General Admission tickets are included in all booth reservations.

🚨Important Info🚨

· Ticket does \*NOT\* include Skate Rental.

· Skates & safety gear are available to rent \*\*first come, first served\*\*

· All sales are final. No refunds.

· You must sign the Xanadu waiver in advance here: https://shorturl.at/AJbHn

· Valid Government ID required for entry. Photos of IDs are not accepted

· Gum, outside food and drink is not allowed.

· All bags are subject to search at the venue entrance.

· Xanadu is wheelchair accessible and includes entry ramps and ADA bathrooms. Write to info@xanadu.nyc if you require extra assistance.

· Xanadu is an inclusive, safe space. We do not tolerate harassment, aggression, racism, bigotry, or hatred of any kind.

Skating is FUN. Skating is RISKY!

Together we will create a skate experience that is fun and safe for everyone on the rink!

· Be mindful of yourself, your limits and others around you.

· Our Skate Guards are always here to help! Please alert them to any hazards or unsafe behavior on the rink so that they can help.

· Rink capacity fluctuates throughout each session- if you are ever feeling overwhelmed, take a quick break and get back into the flow when you’re ready.

· Keep each other safe & happy! Less friction, more FLOW.

More questions? Find answers here: xanadu.nyc/FAQ

✨By purchasing a ticket, you agree to and are bound by Xanadu's Terms and Conditions: https://tinyurl.com/XanaduTermsConditions

*DM @builtbymeanred for group rates and more information*  
  
  
**Regal86**

Regal86 is a DJ producer from Monterrey, Nuevo León, blending the raw energy of rave and club culture with Latin-driven percussion. With over 40 albums released in just a few years, he’s established a distinct underground style.

**10010**

From techno and breaks to salsa and dembow, 1OO1O’s approach to music is always fresh, combining versatile sounds in unique ways. His tracks play at the biggest festivals, clubs, and on radio shows worldwide, while his live sets showcase his love of rare gems, blending new sounds with club classics.  
  

**Shekdash**

NYC-based DJ and producer Shekdash brings high-impact techno and major dancefloor energy to every event. He’s known for his sharp curation skills and deep understanding of club music as a Rinse FM resident. From the club to the airwaves, Shekdash brings endless grooves and energy to the dancefloor.

**1Morning**

LA-bred DJ and producer 1morning blends 90s-rooted intensity with a funky, forward-thinking edge. His vinyl-driven sets and soulful, gritty productions have taken him from LA warehouses to Tresor in Berlin and The White Hotel in Manchester.

On Saturday, November 14th, Cadence welcomes UK producer Seb Wildblood to a secret loft in the heart of Lower Manhattan for a night of rhythm, melody, and something a little stranger than usual.

**THE LINEUP**

Seb Wildblood (UK) - London underground legend - bringing together woozy, soulful synths for the dance floor, with melodies that hit harder than you expect. He's the founder of the early 2010's Church party in South London and the 'All My Thoughts' label. Expect trippy, percussive, and unbelievably danceable grooves.

Delacour (NYC) - One of the best of the best in current NYC talent. Delacour's tracks combine the deepest rhythms with moving melodic undertones. Releases span Deeperfect, Andhera, and recent EP 'In Your Atmosphere.'

Elkind B3B Hugh Zhang B3B RYô - Cadence resident triple threat. We'll be teleporting you away from Manhattan into Jupiter. Or Mars.

Pancho B2B J2 - Setting the tone from the jump.

**THE THEME: THE GREENHOUSE**

This time, we're introducing a new theme to the party: the greenhouse. Take that however you want, but we're turning the loft into a strange little garden after dark.

**ABOUT CADENCE**

2026 has been a year of venturing into the unknown for us, leaning into a newer Balearic sound that's heavy on nostalgia and groove. But as many of you know, we started DIY, and we can't wait to show you what we have in store.

**LOCATION**

Secret loft location, Lower Manhattan (address will be shared with ticket holders day-of show)

**ENTRY & HOUSE POLICY**

Cadence is a space for everyone. We welcome people of all genders, races, sexualities, and backgrounds, and we're committed to keeping the dance floor safe and respectful for all.

Discrimination, harassment, or aggressive behavior of any kind will not be tolerated. Anyone acting against the spirit of the party will be asked to leave.

Entry is at the sole discretion of the door. A ticket does not guarantee admission. Please bring a valid photo ID.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.

If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

raw.description:
With over two decades of electronic music eminence, Eli Escobar has confirmed his place amongst dance music greats. With an unparalleled record collection of handpicked gems and curveball productions, Escobar guides revellers through the heartbeat of music, from the past to the future.

Always looking forward and keeping step with evolving generational tastes, Escobar has redefined his sound in recent years. As an acquainted DJ & Producer, the dance music veteran cut his teeth into the epicentre of 1990’s New York City hedonism and set the foundations for an admirable career. Releasing music on influential labels such as Phonica, Razor n Tape, Defected’s ‘Classic’ and his very own label imprint Night People, only gives a snapshot into the depth of his discovery.

Spanning over more than 20 years, the influence and presence of Eli Escobar is undeniable in every corner of dance music. As a selector he has appeared on a variety of influential platforms including BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix, Resident Advisor's Exchange Podcast, Boiler Room, Mixmag ‘The Lab’ and The Lot Radio, only to name a few. Likewise transporting his sound to dancefloors across the world with residencies at House of Yes, Le Bain, Battlehymn and beyond.

Globally respected and recognised as a forward thinking producer, Escobar’s output steps beyond conventional dance music with remix work for the likes of Lana Del Rey, M.I.A., Honey Dijon, Cakes Da Killa and many more. Now heading into 2023 Eli looks to stay true to his musical progression.

\--
  
Bag Raiders are icons of the Australian dance scene. After dropping cult underground cuts (Fun Punch, Turbo Love, Big Fun), Jack Glass and Chris Stracey signed to Modular Records and released their game-changing, self-titled debut album in 2010, debuting at No. 7 on the ARIA Album Chart and earning nominations from ARIA, triple j and APRA. The LP featured hit singles Way Back Home, Sunlight, Snake Charmer, and the now-legendary Shooting Stars — one of the biggest Australian dance tracks of all time. Shooting Stars has become a global phenomenon, racking up over 4 billion streams, 40+ Platinum and 7 Gold certifications, 18 million Shazams and peaked at No. 11 on Billboard’s Dance chart.

They followed with acclaimed EPs (Waterfalls, Checkmate, Friend Inside) and teamed up with Mayer Hawthorne on Beat Me to the Punch. Their second LP Horizons arrived in 2019, followed by the launch of their label Broken Head Records in 2022 and club-driven releases like Love Me Back and Right Here / Saliba.

In 2023, Troye Sivan sampled Shooting Stars on his Grammy-nominated single Got Me Started, and they dropped collabs with Boston Bun (SAVE ME) and Panama (Flowers).

In 2025 and beyond, Bag Raiders are locked in for a relentless release schedule of club weapons — kicking off with Hold Me, out now on UK label The Cross Records.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Few artists have managed to cultivate name and brand recognition quite like Belgium native, bass music icon, Michael Bella. His cutting edge, high-energy basslines, and masterwork song structures stimulate the senses, complimented by 100% original artwork that ties his unmistakable branding together under his DJ & Producer alias, Eptic.

At an early age Eptic found not only a love for Rock & Metal, but Drum & Bass – the inspiration behind him wanting to learn and produce himself at a mere fourteen years old. Laying the creative fundamentals down at such a young age has paved the way for the now well-known international bass enthusiast, gaining the respect and attention from, and ultimately collaborating with, many well known artists such as DJ Snake, Marshmello, Dillon Francis, Jauz, Juicy J, among others.

Equally known for both his music, off-stage comedy skits, and social media personality, Eptic has secured acclaim far outreaching the bass music community proving there’s no boundaries for the Eptic moniker. With the debut of his fabled “Overlord Stage” at the end of 2021, Bella gave us a thrilling glimpse of what’s in store for 2022.

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Caracas-born DJ and producer Tony Guerra was raised inside the rhythm. Surrounded from an early age by a family of promoters, percussionists, and club selectors, he quickly channeled that musical foundation into electronic music, taking cues from the minimal precision of Ricardo Villalobos and the soulful bounce of classic house heavyweights like Dennis Ferrer and Sandy Rivera.

After breaking out on Caracas's Hot 94 FM and co-founding the influential underground collective The Deep Party, Guerra turned his focus to production, blending raw tech grooves with Afro-Caribbean percussion. With early releases spanning imprints like Fat Line Music and Road Trip Recordings alongside regular international radio appearances, Guerra has established himself as a fixture of the South American circuit, continually taking his rhythm-forward sound to premier clubs and international dancefloors.

Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Space 92 returns to 99 Scott on Saturday, November 28, bringing his high-impact strain of techno back to Brooklyn for a late-night warehouse session with Gray Area.

The French producer has become one of the defining names in peak-time techno, ranking as Beatport’s best-selling Techno Peak Time/Drive artist since 2020 and earning a string of No. 1 records along the way. His sound pulls together trance-charged techno, distorted percussion, acid and flashes of nostalgia inspired by his love of vintage ‘80s sci-fi. His catalog stretches across Drumcode, Filth on Acid, Factory 93 and Arcane, with collaborations alongside Hardwell, HI-LO and Reinier Zonneveld. Remixes for Nicole Moudaber and Layton Giordani have also topped Beatport’s charts.

His latest run keeps that momentum moving with “Proton” alongside Alignment, a remix of Oxia’s “Domino,” “Dimension” on his TAKEOFF imprint and “Free My Soul” with Vini Vici and CERES. Beyond his solo work, Space 92 has joined POPOF for Turbulences, performing together on major festival stages around the world.

Now he returns to 99 Scott, where towering ceilings, exposed brick and an industrial main room set the stage for the kind of heavy, late-night session his music demands. Space 92 has played the Brooklyn warehouse before, and on November 28, he’s coming back for another round.

Tickets are limited. Secure yours and meet us on the dance floor Expect pressure, sci-fi atmosphere and a set built for late-night Brooklyn.

See you 99 Scott.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

As G-House powers forward at a menacing pace, BIJOU is the name on everyone’s lips. Instead of setting the bar for the genre, he only raises it higher. Rather than embracing the standard, he constantly pushes the envelope further with a distinct, robust soundscape all his own.

BIJOU’s show-stopping 2016 collaboration with Dr. Fresch, “Hello” marked a major turning point for his career in music and Future Ghetto as a whole. In the same week, his debut on Night Bass thrust BIJOU to the forefront of the G-House movement and he has never looked back.

His records continue to catch fire, gaining massive support from AC Slater, Destructo, Don Diablo, Drezo, Malaa, Party Favor and many more. BIJOU fed the blaze with a series of ambitious releases including “Gotta Shine” featuring Germ, “Revelation” with Dr. Fresch featuring Denzel Curry, and “Louis V” with modern legend and Night Bass champion AC Slater. BIJOU topped off 2018 with his stellar 4-track Super Phat EP, an instant staple in the modern dance scene. Flash-forward to 2019 and his Gangsta Party EP with Dr. Fresch (DND Records) has primed the producer for yet another successful year.

Infusing elements of hip hop and classic house, BIJOU’s sound is live enough for the underground, but mean enough to hold down any main stage. Fans at EDC Vegas in 2017 witnessed this firsthand as he took over kineticFIELD in full form. He followed up in 2018 with a thrilling Australian run and his first headlining U.S. Super Phat Tour. Having gained all the street cred he needs, BIJOU is now looking worldwide.

Keep your eyes and ears locked on BIJOU — fearless leader, G-House supreme — because he’s about to take over!

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Oliver Smith has been described as "an excellent DJ" by Armin van Buuren, "the best thing to happen in trance" by Mixmag and "sensational" by DJ Magazine. In recent years the popular UK-based DJ and dance music producer has released scores of records and performed at some of the biggest clubs and festivals in the world.

Oliver’s forward thinking music is regularly played by leading DJs such as Above & Beyond, Hardwell, David Guetta, Ferry Corsten and Sander van Doorn. He was the first signing to the Anjunabeats record label and is the only producer (other than label bosses Above & Beyond) to have featured on all 13 ‘Anjunabeats Volume’ compilations to date. Oliver has also been highly successful with remixes for the likes of Arty, Mat Zo, Seven Lions, and Maor Levi - all featuring on leading radio and club play lists and flying high in the Spotify and Beatport charts. In 2018 he mixed the ‘Anjunabeats Worldwide 08’ compilation, which includes ten of his own productions. It reached the #1 spot on the iTunes dance chart in USA, UK, Canada, Australia and more.

As a DJ, Oliver has played at legendary UK venues such as Ministry of Sound, The Warehouse Project and Wembley Arena; and at far flung locations worldwide including America, India, and Ibiza. He has also performed at some of the biggest festivals in the world such as Tomorrowland, EDC Las Vegas, and Creamfields. He is also a regular presenter of Anjunabeats Worldwide Radio, which is broadcast on over 100 FM stations across the planet.

\--

Genix has deep roots in dance music that have helped his production career to grow exponentially since his debut release in 2003. Since then he has become a mainstay of

Anjunabeats, with other releases on Armada, Vandit Records, Enhanced Records and Spinnin Records to name a few. DJing alongside the world’s elite along the way, he has become a huge name in his own right.

A very successful 2024 saw Genix release his second artist album titled YOU.ME.NOW, a stellar follow up to his debut album ‘199X’ which both led to successful global tour dates around the world from Asia, Australia, Europe & USA. The pick of album tracks were played on BBC radio 1 where Genix went on to host his own show as part of an Anjunabeats takeover.

His formidable sound blends the most vibrant elements of trance, techno, house and progressive into a potent, high octane cocktail. With a penchant for in-your-face textures and sounds set against stunning melody and beautiful atmospherics, his sound is at the vanguard of the trance movement. Blending reverence for the formative sounds of a 1990s dance music upbringing with the sounds of now, his tracks are consistently among the most spinetingling in the scene. With no compromise in his style across his 200+ released singles and remixes, he is an artist who is truly dedicated to his scene. Collaborating with and remixing the likes of Armin van Buuren, Above & Beyond, Gabriel & Dresden and Cosmic Gate, he has become part of the fabric of the scene.

He first found fame as a resident and promoter at legendary UK club night Passion, which was one of the epicentres of the ‘90s/2000s trance explosion. Cutting his name alongside the scene’s biggest DJs, he amassed a wealth of knowledge and experience that would give him solid foundations for the rest of his career. By the time he turned his hand to production in the early 2000s, he had a keen understanding of what worked on a dancefloor, giving him a huge head start. It quickly became clear that he was as talented in the studio as behind the decks, and it wasn’t long before he was attracting major attention.

At one point he held the Guinness World Record for the longest DJ set in history, clocking in at 84 hours. He also recently broke the world record for playing a DJ set at the highest recorded land altitude, playing at Mount Everest Base Camp at 5,600 metres above sea level. He has supported Above & Beyond at epic shows across the world including at the New York Expo Centre, The Gorge Amphitheater in Washington and the O2 Arena Prague and laid waste to some of the world’s biggest dance festivals including Tomorrowland, Creamfields, Dreamstate and A State of Trance.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Rising DJ and producer, Capochino has been brewing a genre-bending sound that has been tipping hats from industry veterans and landing him on the map as an artist to watch out for. He made a profound impact with his first track of the year, “Woke Symphony,” premiering on Headbang Society, followed by “Untethered Soul” featuring jean, released on Excision’s Subsidia Records. With each release, Capochino doesn’t just deliver music; he invites listeners to embrace their roots and tell their own stories through their unique creative expressions.

On December 12th, MVSON lands at 99 Scott for a New York takeover bringing the Manchester born event brand and record label to Brooklyn.

MVSON grew out of Manchester’s club scene as a platform for parties, music and the community surrounding both. What began through underground events in the city developed into a wider world of club nights and releases, carrying the character of its beginnings into new cities and venues.

MVSON events have become known for carefully selected lineups, packed rooms and crowds that reflect the open spirit at the center of the brand. Rather than operating as a standard artist led party series, MVSON has developed into a platform of its own, bringing together names from across house and club music while creating space for artists connected to its wider circle.

Alongside the events, MVSON has expanded into a record label, giving the platform another way to introduce music beyond the dance floor. The label serves as a home for releases tied to the sound and culture surrounding the parties.

Now MVSON heads to New York, with 99 Scott becoming the next setting for the UK born brand as its event series and label arrive in Brooklyn for one night.

Built from Manchester club culture and carried outward through its events and releases, MVSON has become a meeting point for artists, records and crowds around it. December 12th marks the next step for the platform as it brings that energy into a well known Brooklyn room.

value.title: How old do I have to be to enter SILO?

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. This includes leering, staring, and cutting off someone else’s ability to move freely.
value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Live aerialists, immersive visuals, and a champagne toast and balloon drop at midnight!  
  
Gravagerz is an Italian DJ, record producer, and songwriter based in Luxembourg. Known for his signature Euphoric House sound, he blends elements of House, UK Garage, and Dubstep into his productions. As an independent artist, Gravagerz has accumulated over 7 million monthly Spotify listeners and more than 300 million combined streams across various platforms. In addition to his solo work, he is a versatile producer, collaborating with hip-hop, pop, K-pop, R&B, and dance artists on their upcoming albums.

In 2020, Gravagerz signed a management contract with Leaf Music Management at the age of 17. His early releases included "Look Back at It" with Tom Field on B1 Recordings, as well as remixes for Regard x Ella Henderson and Era Istrefi. His breakthrough came with "Chihiro", originally a remix of Billie Eilish's song on SoundCloud, which went viral on TikTok and Instagram, amassing over 200 million combined streams and 1.2 million video creators using the track. After replacing the vocals, he officially released it as his own version.  
  
Following this success, he secured an official remix of Quavo and Lana Del Rey’s “Tough” followed by another official cover release of Disclosure and London Grammar’s “Help Me Lose My Mind”, which garnered over 50 million streams and 50,000 video creators on social media.

In April 2025, Gravagerz released “Pool” featuring Kiki Wera, marking his first record to chart in the UK Top 100, reaching 15 million combined streams and inspiring 20,000 video creators.

His remixes frequently go viral on TikTok, with multiple tracks exceeding 50,000 video creators, including Drake’s “Time Flies,” A$AP Rocky’s “Fukk Sleep,” and WizzTheMC’s “Show Me Love."
